text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jordanian aviation official says practical joint work with Israel on "peace airport" in Aqaba not likely to start before beginning of next year because Israel isn't ready to start earlier.
- Amman court orders liquidation of Amman Bank for Investment after losses reached 75 percent of its paid up capital.
- King Hussein's European tour to Italy, Britain, France and Slovenia to start on June 10.
- Labour Ministry source says deadline for expatriate workers to register extended until June 19.
- Professional unions and opposition parties heading toward escalated confrontation with government over press law and lack of implementation of a government agreement on pay.
- Parliamentary election candidates ask government to foot the bill for their election campaigns.
- Egyptian ambassador in Jordan says President Hosni Mubarak noticed positive changes in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during their Sharm al-Sheikh summit.
- Tourism Minister Aqel Beltaji says Qatari team to visit Jordan from June 9-11 to discuss investment opportunities.
- Islamic Action Front parliamentary candidates to be named at the end of June.
- Crown Prince Hassan back home from trip to Europe focused on furthering relations.
